trigger: Live offense values no longer match old crosswalk assumptions.
how_to_detect: Distinct live values fail to join old categories or require new overrides.
promotion_effect: Do not promote until the crosswalk is refreshed.
standard_response: Refresh offense_crosswalk.csv from live values and mark exact versus approximate lines.

trigger: Live date fields changed or older midpoint logic is no longer valid.
how_to_detect: Packet finds different date columns from historical loader assumptions.
promotion_effect: Year assignment can be wrong and every downstream count can drift.
standard_response: Rewrite date logic against the live schema and validate the resulting year totals.

trigger: One or more years in the target window are materially undercovered.
how_to_detect: Year counts show anomalously low totals or code sanity thresholds fail.
promotion_effect: City is not buildable for the intended window.
standard_response: Treat as a source contract problem before any promotion discussion.

trigger: Source contains multiple rows per incident or per incident offense.
how_to_detect: Counts exceed expectation until dedupe is applied or duplicate key values exist.
promotion_effect: Raw and reconciled counts are inflated until dedupe is fixed.
standard_response: Define the dedupe grain explicitly and store it with the offense contract.

trigger: Coordinates are missing or invalid for too many mapped rows.
how_to_detect: Plausible lat or lon share is low or falls below city-specific sanity gates.
promotion_effect: Spatial shares are unsafe for city-wide promotion.
standard_response: Look for source-provided block groups or a retained proxy geography before discarding the city.

trigger: Raw feed has fallback geography but the builder cache stripped it out.
how_to_detect: Packet shows raw fields like beat exist but minimal parquet lacks them.
promotion_effect: Public recovery path is lost inside the live builder path.
standard_response: Expand cache contract or reread the full raw feed in the builder.

trigger: Rows are privacy-redacted and no stable public proxy geography survives.
how_to_detect: Serious offenses have missing or snapped locations with no retained proxy field.
promotion_effect: City-wide promotion is blocked and offense-level promotion may also be blocked.
standard_response: Treat unresolved rows as a bounded public tail only if that tail is small and explicit.

trigger: Feed mixes city incidents with out-of-city or OOJ events.
how_to_detect: Rows carry Out of SF or OOJ like markers or fail city membership joins.
promotion_effect: Counts and shares are inflated if rows are retained.
standard_response: Filter or separately track city-level residuals and never allocate them to block groups.

trigger: Historical and current feeds overlap or change systems midstream.
how_to_detect: Both feeds populate the same year or metadata documents a system break.
promotion_effect: Double-counting or contract gaps persist until cutoff is explicit.
standard_response: Set a hard cutoff date and record overlap behavior in the packet.

packet_integration_hint: Report type distribution shows large supplement volumes and reconciliation improves after filtering.
reusable_fix_pattern: Naive city totals are inflated or unstable.

trigger: Published reference counts a different concept than the public incident feed.
how_to_detect: Packet can only label the comparison approximate or finds offense-count versus incident-count mismatch.
promotion_effect: Approximate lines cannot justify city-wide promotion alone.
standard_response: Use exact-comparable lines as the hard gate and keep approximate lines as support only.

trigger: Large share of rows lacks the field needed for exact offense mapping.
how_to_detect: Null rate on offense code or offense category is materially high.
promotion_effect: Direct mapping is incomplete and may undercount key offenses.
standard_response: Isolate bounded candidate rules and validate them across more than one period before promotion.

trigger: Packet finds an empirical rule that improves reconciliation but the live contract does not document it.
how_to_detect: Candidate rule matches one or two periods closely but lacks source-contract backing.
promotion_effect: Do not promote on the candidate alone.
standard_response: Mark the candidate explicitly and require multi-period validation before central adoption.

trigger: Older city is already live despite gaps that would block a new promotion today.
how_to_detect: Packet notes active use plus ongoing hardening despite material exact-comparable divergence.
promotion_effect: Do not treat the city as the default quality threshold for future promotions.
standard_response: Use it for packet shape and source clues but not as the bar for new city-wide approvals.
